title: Visible Light
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Sciences: Visible Light Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: Light travels in straight lines at very high speed; it can be reflected, absorbed, transmitted and refracted. White light is made of a spectrum of colours that can be separated by a prism; we see objects because light from them enters our eyes. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 8, Energy and Change: Visible light)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): how light travels, reflection, refraction, the spectrum, colour and how we see. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines at about 300 000 km per second. Opaque objects block light and make shadows; transparent materials let light through; translucent materials let some through. We see objects when light from them enters our eyes.

A mirror reflects light: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Light bends (refracts) when it passes from one material to another, such as from air into water. A prism splits white light into the spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

Example

A ray hits a mirror at 40°. What is the angle of reflection?

They are equal.

Answer: 40°

Example

Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

Light changes speed.

Answer: refraction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we see because light leaves our eyes.
  • Thinking white light is one colour.
  • Thinking a red shirt absorbs red light.

faq.q: Why does a red apple look red?
faq.a: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours.
Raindrops refract and split sunlight into its colours.

items.q: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. If a planet were 4 times as far from the Sun as Earth, about how long would sunlight take to reach it?
items.e: Twice as far takes twice as long, and so on.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a glowing computer screen, a lit bulb, the Moon or the Sun?
items.e: The Moon does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Is a metal tray transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A metal tray lets no light through and makes a dark shadow.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a campfire, a lit bulb, a star or the planet Venus?
items.e: The planet Venus does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: The angle of reflection at a plane mirror is 10°. What is the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror surface?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle is 90° − 10° = 80°.

items.q: The angle of reflection at a plane mirror is 80°. What is the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror surface?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle is 90° − 80° = 10°.

items.q: A ray of light makes an angle of 35° with the surface of a mirror. What is the angle of incidence (measured from the normal)?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the mirror surface is 65°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angles are measured from the normal: 90° − 65° = 25°, and i = r.

items.q: A green book is lit only by red light. What colour does it look?
items.e: Objects reflect their own colour and absorb the others. If their colour is not in the light, they look black.

items.q: Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
c: It is laterally inverted (left and right are swapped).
It is real (it can be caught on a screen).
It is larger than the object.
It is not changed from left to right.
items.e: A plane mirror image is upright, the same size, laterally inverted, virtual and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal (at 90° to the surface). What happens or why?
c: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water.
Different colours refract by different amounts.
It goes straight on without bending.
items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: What is refraction?
c: the bending of light as it passes from one material into another
items.e: It changes speed.

items.q: A smooth, polished metal tray shows a clear image. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of regular reflection.

items.q: What is the law of reflection?
c: angle of incidence = angle of reflection

items.q: Ethan drew this diagram to explain how we see the flower. Is it correct?
c: It is missing the light travelling from the source to the object.
It shows the source being seen, not how light from the object reaches the eye.
